meta.title: UK public sector AI guidance sources
meta.description: Candidate sources to incorporate into the AI Guidance Explorer. Each entry is structured for humans and LLMs to scan, filter, and cite.

already_incorporated.title: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
already_incorporated.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
already_incorporated.notes: Currently powers the FAQ answers and citations on the explorer.

fields.id: Stable slug for linking and imports
fields.title: Official document or collection title
fields.type: guidance | standard | framework | code_of_practice | action_plan | regulator_guidance
fields.why_include: Why this source matters for the explorer
fields.related_faq_themes: Existing FAQ categories it would help answer

sources.title: Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) Hub
sources.summary: Hub for the ATRS template, completion guidance, scope/exemptions policy, and published records of algorithmic tools used in public-sector decision making.
sources.why_include: Mandatory transparency requirement referenced throughout the AI Playbook; answers questions about when and how to publish algorithmic tool records.

sources.title: Guidance on AI and data protection
sources.summary: ICO guidance on applying UK data protection law to AI systems that process personal data, including fairness, bias, security, and Article 22 considerations.
sources.why_include: Primary regulator view for personal-data FAQs (DPIAs, lawful basis, automated decisions, fairness).

sources.title: Guidelines for secure AI system development
sources.summary: Practical security guidelines across secure design, development, deployment, and operation/maintenance of AI systems.
sources.why_include: Deepens playbook security answers (poisoning, leakage, prompt injection, secure deployment patterns).

sources.title: Guidelines for AI procurement
sources.organisation: Government Digital Service (GDS) / historically Office for AI and DCMS/DSIT
sources.summary: Best-practice guidance for public-sector buyers on preparing, specifying, evaluating, awarding and managing AI procurements.
sources.why_include: Core source for buy-vs-build, requirements, lock-in, and ethics-in-procurement FAQs.

sources.title: Data and AI Ethics Framework
sources.summary: Principles and practical activities for responsible development, procurement and use of data and AI in the public sector, with an accompanying self-assessment tool.
sources.why_include: Bridges high-level ethics principles to project actions; complements ATRS and procurement guidance.

sources.title: Ethics, Transparency and Accountability Framework for Automated Decision-Making
sources.organisation: Cabinet Office / DSIT / Office for AI (as published)
sources.summary: Seven-point framework for safe, sustainable and ethical use of solely automated and AI-assisted decision-making in government, plus a risk potential assessment form.
sources.why_include: Directly answers FAQs on automated decisions, responsibility, contestability and lawful operation of ADM.

sources.title: Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
sources.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
sources.summary: Voluntary code setting baseline cyber security requirements across AI design, development, deployment, maintenance and end of life; intended to inform emerging standards.
sources.why_include: Complements NCSC guidelines with a lifecycle code of practice useful for supplier and assurance questions.

sources.title: Introduction to AI assurance
sources.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) – Responsible Technology Adoption Unit
sources.summary: Accessible introduction to AI assurance concepts, techniques (impact assessment, audit, testing) and how to embed assurance in organisational practice.
sources.why_include: Supports FAQs on quality assurance, monitoring, evidence of fitness-for-purpose and governance boards.

sources.title: AI Opportunities Action Plan
sources.organisation: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
sources.summary: Government roadmap and response on accelerating beneficial AI adoption, including scan/pilot/scale approaches and smarter public-sector procurement.
sources.why_include: Strategic context for why government is adopting AI and how procurement and scaling may change; useful for leadership FAQs.

sources.title: Responsibly buying AI: a guide for councils in England
sources.organisation: Local Government Association (LGA), with LOTI, EHRC and ICO
sources.summary: Role-based prompts for English councils to embed Public Sector Equality Duty and data protection into AI commissioning, procurement and contract management.
sources.why_include: Extends coverage beyond central government to local public sector buyers; strong equality + DP angle.
